source.title: Dynamic shifts of limited working memory resources in human vision

confidence_rationale: The canonical statement of the FLEXIBLE-resource horn of Q-077's fork, and the one the claim's own notes flag as MIXED against SD-046. It supports the resource model (no fixed item limit; a shared resource distributed by a power law; the acted-on/attended item drawing disproportionate precision) -- which directly problematises SD-046's discrete-slot framing, while remaining consistent with SD-046 holding N>=2 goals at graded fidelity. Marked mixed rather than weakens because it undercuts the DISCRETE parameterisation without contradicting the multi-slot design decision itself; confidence moderate because it is visual-WM precision, not goal maintenance, and the result is actively contested (Zhang & Luck 2008, Cowan & Rouder 2009).
failure_signatures: The power-law resource model predicts NO hard cutoff, so a discrete-slot SD-046 would produce a step function the resource account says cannot exist; if the arena shows smooth precision dilution instead, SD-046's fixed-N framing is wrong.

The result is contested: Zhang & Luck (2008) and Cowan & Rouder (2009) argue a slots-plus-averaging / item-limit model fits the same data at least as well, so Bays & Husain cannot unilaterally settle the fork -- the discriminating experiment must be run on REE's own substrate.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Visual working memory is not fixed by a number of objects but is a limited resource shared dynamically across all items in a scene; the proportion of resource allocated to an item sets the precision with which it is remembered (a power-law relation), and allocation is biased by selective attention and toward saccade targets.
mapping.ree_translation: Q-077's resource horn: SD-046's multi-slot GoalState could be a single flexible precision budget shared across goals, with each added goal diluting the budget (smooth power-law degradation) and the acted-on/attended goal drawing disproportionate precision. Bays & Husain is the primary evidence for this reading, and its 'attention/saccade-target draws more resource' finding maps onto Q-077's 'acted-on goal draws disproportionate fidelity' sub-prediction.
mapping.mapping_caveat: This is visual working-memory PRECISION for briefly-remembered items, not maintenance of active goals with drive coupling and persistence. The transfer from per-item visual precision to per-goal behavioural/representational fidelity is a genuine gap. Marked MIXED (per Q-077's notes) because it problematises the DISCRETE-slot framing while remaining consistent with the multi-slot design decision (N>=2 goals at graded fidelity); it is not a clean weakens of SD-046 as a whole.
mapping.source_context: Human psychophysics; visual working memory report tasks with analogue (continuous) response measures; set-size and saccade-target manipulations.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality high (Science; rigorous analogue-report psychophysics) but tempered by an active, published dispute (Zhang & Luck 2008; Cowan & Rouder 2009 comment + Bays & Husain 2009 reply, both in this literature). Mapping fidelity 0.55: the resource construct and the attention-draws-precision finding map well to Q-077, but visual-item precision != goal maintenance. Transfer risk 0.50 reflects that gap plus the unresolved status of the resource-vs-slot debate in the source field itself.
